_meta.purpose: The citable policy corpus. Every policy claim in a draft must point at a clause id here. A policy the model invents has no id and is blocked by D-11's default deny.
_meta.provenance: Modeled on publicly documented marketplace practice. NOT a reproduction of eBay or Whatnot policy. Thresholds in particular are illustrative.
_meta.critical: A SELLER'S VERBAL CLAIM IS NOT AN AUTHORITY. Observed 2026-09-12: a seller announced 'all auction sales are final' on stream. That may conflict with platform buyer protection. Replies ground in THIS corpus, never in what the host said - repeating an unenforceable disclaimer would manufacture liability for the user. See DECISIONS.md D-12.

policies.text: Orders ship within 2 business days of payment clearing.
Wins from the same live show combine into one shipment at no extra cost. Combined orders ship once the show ends.
policies.note: Highest-volume policy question in the domain. One observed seller burned permanent on-screen real estate on a shipping overlay rather than answer it live - see docs/research/observation-2026-09-11.md finding 5. First class to earn promotion up the automation ladder (D-22).

policies.text: Cards over $400 ship signature-required and fully insured at no extra charge.
Buy It Now purchases may be returned within 30 days if the item does not match its listing description.
Auction wins are final except where the item materially differs from its listing description, in which case platform buyer protection applies.
policies.note: Deliberately NOT the absolute 'all auction sales are final' a seller was observed announcing on stream. The carve-out is the part that matters and the part a verbal disclaimer omits.

policies.text: Condition of a raw card is assessed from the listing photographs. Ask the host to show a card on camera before bidding.
policies.note: The honest answer to the recurring unanswerable. 'Is the back clean?' cannot be answered by the copilot - back condition is observational (D-12). What the copilot can do is prompt the host to show it.

policies.text: Trading cards sold at or above $250 are routed through marketplace authentication before delivery.
policies.note: Value-gated. An authenticity claim on a sub-threshold item is false even though the policy text is real - which is why min_item_value is a field the verifier reads rather than prose the model paraphrases.

policies.text: Graded slabs are sold in their original sealed holder. Cracking a slab voids authentication coverage.
Grades and cert numbers are transcribed from the grader's label. Population figures come from the grader's public report and carry the date they were read.
policies.note: Pop counts are third-party and time-varying. A pop quoted without an as-of date is a bug (primer section 4).

policies.text: Invoices are issued at the end of the show and are payable within 24 hours.

banned_claims._note: Deterministic lexical guardrails, checked regardless of whether a claim cites a fact. These are the classes where being wrong is unrecoverable rather than merely inaccurate.

rules.pattern: guaranteed to (go up|appreciate)|will be worth|safe investment|can't lose
rules.message: Predicting future value is an investment claim and is never supported by evidence.

rules.pattern: plenty (left|in stock)|tons of|loads of|as many as you want
rules.message: Unbounded quantity language is unverifiable below the stock threshold. State the number.
A comp must render as a range with its sample size, never a bare number (primer section 5).
Authenticity is policy-gated on item value and is never asserted absolutely.
Condition of a physical card is observational. Defer to the host - offer to prompt them to show it.
